steps.title: Dry Furmint
steps.body: Dry Furmint's acidity and texture suit rich fish, roast chicken, pork, goose, and creamy Hungarian dishes like chicken paprikash. Its smoky, mineral side suits smoked fish and mushrooms. Serve at 10 to 12 degrees.

steps.title: Tokaji Aszú
steps.body: Aszú suits foie gras, blue cheese, fruit tarts, apricot desserts and even spicy Asian food. Its acidity keeps it fresh with rich food. Serve at 10 to 12 degrees. It ages for decades: Aszú from the 18th century has been found still drinkable.
steps.highlight: Foie gras, blue cheese, apricot tarts

steps.prompt: Match each Furmint wine to a pairing.
steps.explanation: Furmint offers a wine for many courses.

steps.body: Louis XIV is said to have called Tokaji the wine of kings and the king of wines. It was served at European courts for centuries.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dry Furmint suits paprikash, pork and smoked fish
Aszú suits foie gras, blue cheese and fruit desserts
Both are served at 10 to 12 degrees and age well
